proof:
Source: steps 2–4 of the supplied cone_area proof (differentiability, injective derivative and injectivity of G(t, α) = tγ(α)), carried out directly on ℝ × ℝ.
Notation: J := (r₀ − s, r₀ + s), I := (−s, s), R := J × I, G(q) := q.1·γ(q.2) for q ∈ ℝ × ℝ, γ′ := deriv γ.

1. (Positivity.) If (t, α) ∈ R then t > r₀ − s > 0, because s < r₀.

2. (G is injective on R.) Let (t, α), (t′, α′) ∈ R with tγ(α) = t′γ(α′).
- Take norms. Using ‖cv‖ = |c|‖v‖, ‖γ(α)‖ = ‖γ(α′)‖ = 1 and t, t′ > 0 (step 1) gives t = t′.
- Then tγ(α) = tγ(α′) with t ≠ 0 gives γ(α) = γ(α′), by cancelling a nonzero scalar in a real vector space.
- Injectivity of γ on I gives α = α′.
Hence (t, α) = (t′, α′).

3. (γ is differentiable on I.) Let α ∈ I. Since γ is C¹ on I, it is differentiable on I (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn with 1 ≤ 1). I is open and contains α, so it is a neighbourhood of α and γ is differentiable at α. Thus γ has derivative γ′(α) at α (HasDerivAt γ (γ′(α)) α).

4. (Derivative of G.) Fix z = (t, α) ∈ R.
- The first projection π₁(q) = q.1 has derivative fst : (a, b) ↦ a.
- By the chain rule, γ ∘ π₂ (with π₂(q) = q.2) has derivative L₂ : (a, b) ↦ b·γ′(α) at z. Here the derivative of γ at α, viewed as a continuous linear map ℝ → ℝ^P, is c ↦ c·γ′(α), and it is composed with snd.
- By the product rule for a scalar function times a vector function (HasFDerivAt.smul), G = π₁·(γ ∘ π₂) has derivative L := t·L₂ + fst(·)·γ(α) at z, i.e. L(a, b) = t b γ′(α) + a γ(α).
Therefore G is differentiable at z and DG(z) = fderiv ℝ G z = L (HasFDerivAt.fderiv).

5. (Coordinate values.)
- L(1, 0) = t·0·γ′(α) + 1·γ(α) = γ(α) = γ(z.2).
- L(0, 1) = t·1·γ′(α) + 0·γ(α) = tγ′(α) = z.1·γ′(z.2).

6. (DG(z) is injective.) L is linear, so it suffices to show that L(a, b) = 0 implies (a, b) = (0, 0). Suppose t b γ′(α) + a γ(α) = 0.
- Take the inner product with γ(α). Since ⟨γ(α), γ′(α)⟩ = 0 and ⟨γ(α), γ(α)⟩ = ‖γ(α)‖² = 1, this gives t b·0 + a·1 = 0, so a = 0.
- Then (t b)γ′(α) = 0 with γ′(α) ≠ 0 gives t b = 0, and t > 0 (step 1) gives b = 0.

7. (Conclusion.) Step 2 shows G is injective on R. Steps 4–6 show that for every z ∈ R, G is differentiable at z, DG(z) is injective, DG(z)(1, 0) = γ(z.2) and DG(z)(0, 1) = z.1·γ′(z.2). The hypothesis 0 < s is not used. ∎
